findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the coffee bar triple sink uses Bleach (Chlorine) but they do not have test strips to measure the concentration of Chlorine in the triple sink. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and acquired test strips during the inspection. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizing solution can be accurately determined with a test kit or other device
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following areas with an accumulation of soil residues:
(i) Back area staircase storage area has dust hanging from the walls.
(ii) 1ST REPEAT: Dairy walk-in cooler shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iii) Dairy walk-in cooler floor underneath the shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iv) Vents in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of dust.
(v) Bottom grates in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of soil residues.
PIC was notified, and stated that several of these areas are due for cleaning soon. PIC will have these areas cleaned by the next routine inspection. Ensure that Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Coffee: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Coffee: Observed multiple wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. The employee working was educated and the wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wiping cloths are always held in sanitizing solutions between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION.

Coffee: Observed powders for drinks stored with the scoop handles in direct contact with the powder. The employee was educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must be stored to prevent contamination. The inspector suggests storing the scoops outside of the container. Ensure that scoops are stored with the handles above the top of the powder by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Back area: Observed the shelving in the back area walk-in cooler (connected to the dairy display coolers) have an accumulation of debris on the shelves for the dairy display cases. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Bakery: Observed the walk-in freezer floors have an accumulation of food residue underneath the shelving. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the floors are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed four cans of corn that had expired on 09/28/2024 on the shelves. These cans were removed from the shelf and moved to the back during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of checking expiration dates to ensure that foods are safe and honestly presented.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed scoops stored with the handles directly in powders. The powder goes into drinks without cooking or any other kill step for bacteria. The inspector discussed with the employee who moved the scoops into a position where the handles were not in contact with the powders. The scoops must to stored in this position at all times. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Cut room: Observed the ice machine has an accumulation of soil residue on the inside (upper left side). The ice machine must be cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will return on 10/15/2024 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned. 


4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Retail: Observed rotisserie chickens stored in a heat lamp table below 135F. The rotisserie chickens had internal temperatures between 108F to 111F. Hot foods must be hot held at 135F or above. The chickens had been on the table since about 9am. The rotisserie chickens were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. 

For information about the equipment see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed milk and half & half opened more than 24 hours ago lacking proper date marks. The employee working stated the milk and half & half were opened several days ago. The inspector educated the employee and both containers were date marked during the inspection. Ensure that foods held at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Retail: Observed rotisserie chickens stored in a heat lamp table below 135F. The ambient air temperature of the table surface was about 137F which the PIC stated is significantly lower than the usual temperature. The PIC will be scheduling immediate service. Rotisserie chickens (or any other temperature control for safety foods) CANNOT be stored in the heat lamp table until it is serviced and hot holding foods at 135F or above. The inspector will return on 10/15/2024 to ensure the heat lamp table is functioning. 

For information about the food see violation #21.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available in the entire coffee area. The inspector educated the employee about the importance of sanitizer buckets for wiping surfaces. They also discussed the proper procedure for cleaning dishes (wash-rinse-sanitize). The manager filled up a sanitizer bucket for the coffee area from the bakery sanitizer dispenser during the inspection. The employee was instructed to fill up the bucket at the bakery everyday and check the bucket consistently using test strips. It should be dumped and remade on a regular basis. They were also instructed to transfer sanitizer from the bakery to the triple sink when washing dishes. The manager stated they have been working on getting a sanitizer dispenser installed in the coffee area. The inspector encourages that a dispenser be installed or sanitizer containers/tablets are available in the coffee area. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Bakery: Observed the drawer under the prep table holding clean utensils was soiled with food debris. The bakery employee cleaned the drawer during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
